{{nihongo|'''Mio Shrine'''|水尾神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

=== Enshrined God ===
The following two deities are enshrined. </ref>.
* '''{{ill|Iwatsukiwake no Mikoto|ja|磐衝別命|qid=Q11587884}}'''
*: The 11th {{ill|Emperor Suinin|Q314850|qid=Q314850}} prince. In ``Ki|Q813935}}'', he is described as the ancestor of Mio-kun (Mio clan) and Hakui-kun (Hakui clan).{{Sfn|Mizuo Shrine (Gods)|1986|p=353-355}}.
*: Deity enshrined at Kanan Shrine (south main shrine: current shrine).
* '''Himegami''
*: Refers to {{ill|Furihime|Q28415396|qid=Q28415396}}, the mother of the 26th {{ill|Emperor Keitai|Q349277|qid=Q349277}}.
*: He is the enshrined deity of Kahoku Shrine (North Main Hall), and was transferred to Kanan Shrine in 1971|Q2475}} in 1946 ({{ill|1971|Q2475|qid=Q2475}}), where he was enshrined there.

As for the enshrined deities, there were once {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|Q3090037|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko no Mikoto}} (Kanansha), {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|Q462803|qid=Q462803|lt=Tencho Onna no Mikoto}} (Kahoku There was a theory that there were two deities enshrined at the shrine, {{Sfn|Mizuo Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}}, but the shrine is said to enshrine the ancestral deity of Mio-kun, and the two deities currently enshrined are Iwakushibetsu-no-Mikoto and Hime-kami.

</div></div>Mizuo Shrine used to consist of two shrines, Konan-sha (south main shrine) and Kahoku-sha (northern main shrine), which were separated by the Mizuo River, but now it consists of one shrine. The shrine biography <ref group="note">The {{ill|Pratītyasamutpāda|Q522046|qid=Q522046}} of Mizuo Shrine is based on the ``Sanbi Daimyojin Mainland Chronicle'' <sub>Mama</sub> written by Waniko Yasutoshi, an ascetic monk in the early modern period. In {{Harv|Mizuo Shrine (Gods)|1986|p=354}}</ref>, it is said that {{ill|Iwatsukiwake no Mikoto|ja|磐衝別命|qid=Q11587884}} came to live in the place where Sarutahiko no Mikoto is enshrined in order to learn Tensei Shinto of {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|Q3090037|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko no Mikoto}}. name="historical book"/>. Since he worshiped Mio Daimyojin (Nagata Shrine in Nagata, Takashima City) in the morning and evening, where Sarutahiko no Mikoto was enshrined, this place was called ``Haido'' (later Haido), and the site of his residence was called ``Haisho Gosho''. Since Iwashibetsu no Mikoto died in this area, his son, Iwaki Betsuo, buried Iwashibetsu no Mikoto on Mt. Mt. Mt. Mt. Mio, and founded Kanan-sha Shrine (present-day shrine) to enshrine Iwashibetsu no Mikoto.Subsequently, according to the shrine's biography, the 11th prince of Emperor Ojin, Hayaso Betsuno, also came to the area to learn Tensei Shinto, and his fourth grandson, {{ill|Hikoushi no Ōkimi|Q11487892|qid=Q11487892}}, adopted Furihime, the 5th grandson of Iwaki Betsuno, as his wife. Furihime is said to have given birth to three children at the same time, Amaatobe, Otoatobe, and Taitobe (Oatobe, referring to the 26th Emperor Keitai) at the shrine of Mizuo Shrine. It is said that when the child was born, King Hikoshu built a temporary shrine to pray for a safe delivery, and later, King Tenkabu built Mienari Shrine to enshrine his parents on the site of the temporary shrine, which was the beginning of ``Kahoku Shrine'', and after that, the shrine came to enshrine only the god Hime (Furihime). This Kahoku Shrine collapsed in 1971, so it has now been moved to Kana Shrine (current location).

=== Precincts ===
[[File:Mio-jinja (Takashima) honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main shrine/middle gate}}]]
The main shrine is a one-ken shrine {{ill|Nagare-zukuri|Q210684|qid=Q210684}}<ref name="Shrine Hall"/>. In front of the main hall, a worship hall is built across the middle gate. The worship hall is {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}}<ref name="Shrine Hall"/>. Additionally, within the precincts, the Japanese-style garden ``Mizuo Garden'' was completed in {{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}}8 ({{ill|1996|Q2070|qid=Q2070}}).

In addition, there are remains of {{ill|6th century|Q8090|qid=Q8090}} group of tombs (Haido tumulus group) in the mountains behind the precincts, and among them, Ojizuka is said to be the tomb of the ancestor of the Three-Tailed Prince.

=== Related locations ===
* Kitahonden Ruins
** Location: Kamiaido, Takashima City ({{Coord|35|18|45.78|N|135|59|6.86|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|name=Kitahonden Ruins}})
*: Kahokusha (northern main hall) ruins. It was destroyed by a typhoon in 1971 ({{ill|1971|Q2475|qid=Q2475}}), so it was relocated to Kanan Shrine (currently Mizuo Shrine). A stone monument was erected at the site, but it was later moved so there are no remains <ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20140513010549/http://www.geocities.jp/engisiki/oumi/bun/oum221201-02.html Mizuo Shrine North Main Hall (Old Site)] (Investigation of Engishiki Shrine <Personal Site>). </ref>.
* Nagata Shrine
** Location: Nagata, Takashima City ({{Coord|35|18|23.31|N|136|0|25.92|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|name=Nagata Shrine (Mio Daimyojin)}})
*: Shikinaisha. <ref name="Yoshisho"/> is said to be the "Mio Daimyojin" that Iwashibetsu no Mikoto worshiped morning and evening.
* Otaki Shrine
** Location: Otowa, Takashima City ({{Coord|35|17|59.87|N|136|0|5.15|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|name=Osui Shrine (Osuiden Ruins)}})*: It is said to be the ruins of the large cooking hall of Mizuo Shrine {{Sfn|Mizuo Shrine (Gods)|1986|p=353-355}}. It is also said that the large stone at the head of the shrine is the cornerstone of the first torii gate of Mizuo Shrine {{Sfn|Mizuo Shrine (Gods)|1986|p=353-355}}.
* Ota Shrine
** Location: Aoyagi, Azumigawa-cho, Takashima City ({{Coord|35|20|0.08|N|136|1|55.57|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|name=Ota Shrine (Otabisho)}})
*: Formerly known as "Shingu Shrine" <ref name="Hiroki"/>. It is said that it was a tourist place for Mizuo Shrine, and its distance from Mizuo Shrine indicates its former power.{{Sfn|Mizuo Shrine (Gods)|1986|p=353-355}}
* Miou Shrine
** Location: Tokiwagi, Azumigawa-cho, Takashima City ({{Coord|35|20|38.59|N|136|0|33.14|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|name=Mieio Shrine}})
*: Shikinaisha. The deities enshrined are Hikoshu-o and Furi-hime. The company name ``Mieusei'' is said to be derived from the three children Furihime gave birth to.
* Safe delivery leaning stone
** Location: Tanaka, Azumigawa-cho, Takashima City ({{Coord|35|20|18.84|N|136|0|29.06|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|name=Easy delivery leaning stone (Furihime birth legend place)}})
*: Legendary place where Furihime gave birth to her triplet children.
* {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tanakaozuka Tumulus}} (Azumi Mausoleum reference site)** Location: Tanaka, Azumigawa-cho, Takashima City ({{Coord|35|20|24.57|N|136|0|24.07|E|region:JP-25_type:landmark|name=Tanakaozuka Tumulus (Azumi Mausoleum reference site, Hikoshu King's tomb tradition site)}})
*: Legendary site of Hikoshu King's Tomb.

=== Historical evidence ===
[[File:Mio-jinja (Otsu), shaden.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Mio Shrine ({{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}{{ill|Ōtsu|Q202907|qid=Q202907}})}}]]
A shrine that is presumed to be related to Mizuo Shrine is {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}{{ill|Ōtsu|Q202907|qid=Q202907}}{{jalink| {{Sfn|Mizuo Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}}, which is known as {{ill|Mio Shrine|Q65247874|qid=Q65247874}}, the god of landowners, is located near Onjoji Temple|Q1756307}}. According to ``Koshichi Shiryaku,'' the company enshrines three gods that washed up in Otsu from Miozaki, Takashima District on spiritual materials {{Sfn|Mizuo Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}}. From this, it has been pointed out that there is a connection with Mizuo Shrine, and it has also been pointed out that the ``Ōmi Province Three Tailed God'' that appears in historical materials may refer to this place {{Sfn|Mizuo Shrine (Heibonsha)|1991}}.
